name: Septate Uterus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification

criteria.description: Identification of a fibrous or muscular septum dividing the uterine cavity by 3D ultrasound or sonohysterography
Visualization and confirmation of the septum via hysteroscopy
MRI demonstrating normal external uterine contour with internal division consistent with septate uterus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a uterine cavity divided by a fibrous or muscular septum with normal external uterine contour confirmed by imaging or hysteroscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from bicornuate uterus is essential due to differing management

pathognomonic.symptomName: Divided uterine cavity detected on imaging
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic finding on 3D ultrasound or MRI
searchTerms: uterus divided into two cavities on imaging
split uterine cavity seen on scan

pathognomonic.notes: Common clinical presentation in affected women
searchTerms: loss of pregnancy in early weeks

common.notes: Frequently reported in women with septate uterus
Less common than first-trimester loss but significant

occasional.notes: May occur due to uterine abnormalities
searchTerms: pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle

occasional.notes: Some patients diagnosed during infertility workup

rare.notes: Very rare but serious obstetric complication

imaging: 3D transvaginal ultrasound showing uterine cavity division
MRI demonstrating normal external uterine contour with internal septum
other: Laparoscopic assessment to differentiate from bicornuate uterus

distinguishingFeatures: External uterine contour is concave or indented in bicornuate uterus
Two separate uterine horns with a deep fundal cleft
Septate uterus has normal external contour with internal division
Broad, smooth uterine cavity indentation without a fibrous septum
No significant division of uterine cavity
Generally asymptomatic and normal reproductive outcomes

redFlags: Recurrent pregnancy loss without other identifiable cause
Severe dysmenorrhea unresponsive to medical therapy
Inability to conceive after prolonged attempts
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ESHRE/ESGE consensus on the classification of female genital tract congenital anomalies. Hum Reprod. 2013.
Grimbizis GF, et al. The septate uterus: diagnosis and management. Fertil Steril. 2016.
